rationale: This empirical study evaluates a 31.51% municipal water tariff increase under an increasing block tariff (IBT) cross-subsidy structure in Manaus, Brazil, using a natural experiment comparing monthly household water consumption between 2003 and 2004. It clearly meets all eligibility criteria: household municipal water service (C1), a tariff and cross-subsidy pricing rule governing water access and affordability (C2 narrow and plain), quantitative empirical analysis (C3), and household water consumption quantity outcomes (C4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: No divergence: increasing block tariffs, cross-subsidy design and a formal municipal tariff increase squarely satisfy both the narrow rule-type reading (tariff/cost-recovery/subsidy mechanism) and the plain Criterion 2 wording.

evidence_quotes.quote: Increasing block tariffs seek a cross-subsidy mechanism between the water network users, based on the common assumption of weak water price elasticity.

In Manaus, the capital city of the Brazilian state of Amazonas where most of the 1.6 million dwellers are supplied through the municipal water network, a substantial consumption drop followed the tariff increase of 2004.

We see this 31.51% tariff increase as a natural experiment applied to the whole network user population of Manaus and this allows us to measure the impact on monthly consumption of metered households, using month per month differences between years 2003 and 2004.
